memory_model.notes: Transpiles to Python; relies on Python's reference-counting + cycle GC. Substitutions are short-lived dicts that fall out of scope between solutions; the knowledge base persists for the lifetime of the compiled program.

design_notes: Hand-written reference spec for logic_like + dynamic + host_gc. Pragmatic Prolog subset: facts, rules, queries, chronological backtracking via depth-first search.

Subset edges (v1): no cut (!), no dynamic assert/retract, no DCG syntax, no constraint logic, no tabling, no operator declarations, no read/input, no exception machinery (throw/catch). See LOGICLANG_DESIGN.md for the full design.
Iteration is recursion: there are no while/for loops. Multi-clause predicates with mutually exclusive guards replace if/else; recursive predicates with a base case replace for/while.
Closures via partial application: call/2 and call/3 build new goals by appending args to a partial goal term. `call(add(5), 3, R)` constructs `add(5, 3, R)` and solves it.
origin_story: A hand-built reference compiler in the logic-programming family. Used as the template for every logic_like language Forge generates.
